open_points.subject: A10 rule 7 request_digest coverage
open_points.text: "the request an approval covers is described, before sending, by: ... every header the kernel sends"
open_points.question: Which headers are part of that set for digest comparison: only headers explicitly built by kernel rules, or also transport/client-added headers (for example Host, Content-Length, User-Agent, boundary-dependent headers)?
options: Only headers explicitly specified by Cabinet rules (required headers, credential header name, and content headers the kernel itself sets)
All headers present on the wire, including HTTP client/runtime auto-added headers
open_points.default_guess: Only headers explicitly constructed by kernel logic, excluding client/runtime implicit headers.

open_points.subject: A09 rule 2 multipart/form-data construction
open_points.text: "a multipart/form-data body with one part per other input port ... a file part carrying its port's media type, a value part carrying its canonical JSON"
open_points.question: What exact multipart part metadata must be emitted (for example Content-Disposition filename parameter, per-part Content-Type for value parts, charset), and are these details required to be stable for approval matching?
options: Define a fixed canonical multipart part header set and forbid extra metadata
Leave multipart formatting to HTTP library defaults
open_points.default_guess: Define and use a fixed minimal part format (no filename unless explicitly required, stable headers) so request_digest behavior stays deterministic.

open_points.subject: A10 standing grants on non-stopping classes
open_points.text: A10 rule 5: "A grant is given only for a node ... whose effect class is not `destructive`"; A10 rule 1: only `state-transition`, `external-effect` and (exceptionally) resend-after-`not_applied` paths consult approval/grant authority.
open_points.question: Are standing grants for `read` or normal `draft-write` nodes valid and storable (but inert), or should such grant requests be refused as nonsensical?
options: Allow grants for any non-destructive class, even if they have no runtime effect
Refuse grants except for classes that can otherwise block on owner approval
open_points.default_guess: Refuse grants for nodes that never block for approval (read and ordinary draft-write).

open_points.subject: A18 store-call failure behavior
open_points.text: "a link found later makes that store call fail with nothing written"
open_points.question: When such a store call fails during run advancement or owner actions, must the kernel return a refusal and keep running, or terminate process (like A03 cleanup failure), or mark affected runs specially?
options: Return operation failure/internal refusal, keep process alive
Treat as fatal integrity error and stop process
Mark run failed and continue serving
open_points.default_guess: Treat as fatal integrity error and stop process to avoid continuing on a compromised store path.
